extracted.intended_audience: patent owners (inventors, businesses, universities) considering infringement enforcement, sale, or licensing
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for evaluating possible patent infringement and producing claim charts: how to identify possible infringing products, rank their likelihood of infringement, assemble two-column claim charts pairing claim language with documentary evidence, and decide whether to pursue enforcement or sale/licensing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof on the patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: The owner of the patent is entitled under law to compensation for the infringement of the patent, but the burden of proof that there is infringement is on the patent owner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is no public 'patent police'—patent owners must conduct their own investigation, collect evidence, and file a lawsuit; documenting infringement is essential before pursuing enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: What constitutes infringement (reads on an Independent Claim)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a product to be infringing a patent, the product must 'read' on all aspects of at least one Independent Claim in the patent, and the patent owner must be able to prove it – that is, document it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infringement must be shown against every element of an independent claim (the product must meet every claim limitation). Documentation must map product features to claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Chart format (two-column mapping)
rubrics_metrics.description: A Claim Chart is typically a two-column format document in which one of the Independent Claims from the patent appears on the left with the specific section of the Claim that has been infringed highlighted or set apart. On the right side of the page, directly across from the Claim, appears evidence that the infringing product does, indeed, 'read' on that Claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each claim element should be set apart and directly paired with corresponding documentary evidence in the opposite column to show how the product practices that element.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality and types of evidence to include
rubrics_metrics.description: Evidence should show that the infringing product practices each claim element; historically this evidence comes from product literature, advertisements, catalogs, user manuals, tech notes and other documents; today much of it is available online.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully research and locate the 'smoking gun' documentation. Use authoritative sources (official manuals, datasheets, marketing materials, public filings) and capture specific excerpts that map to claim language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Infringement Analysis: scope and ranking
rubrics_metrics.description: This service studies all possibly infringing products submitted by the patent owner, but also spreads out to concentric products. The analysis comes up with a list of possible infringing products, and ranks each as having a Low, Medium or High probability of infringing the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the analysis to focus resources—prioritize High-probability targets for full Claim Chart development and avoid spending time on unlikely infringers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deciding how many Claim Charts to develop
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the results of the Initial Infringement Analysis the patent owner decides which specific products to have fully researched and documented as infringing the product in the form of Claim Charts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: You will not know how many Claim Charts you need until you review the analysis; you may order one or two initially and then order additional charts based on results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and use of Claim Charts (litigation and monetization)
rubrics_metrics.description: With a Claim Chart – or several Claim Charts because there are multiple infringers – a patent owner can engage a law firm or contract with a patent assertion firm to pursue the infringers and seek compensation for infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strong, well-documented Claim Charts are necessary to engage enforcement professionals and can be a basis for licensing, assertion campaigns, or sale; they materially increase the patent's enforceability and market value.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to engage legal/enforcement professionals
rubrics_metrics.description: IPOfferings is a patent brokerage firm. We help our clients sell, license or otherwise monetize their patents. We are NOT attorneys and IPOfferings is NOT a law firm. So when there is documented evidence of infringement, we’ve gone as far as we can go with a patent in terms of its infringement. It is time to turn the patent over to patent enforcement professionals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat broker-conducted analyses and claim charts as preparatory work; actual assertion and litigation decisions require patent litigation counsel or patent assertion firms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative strategy: monetize rather than litigate
rubrics_metrics.description: Rather than endure the risks of filing a patent infringement lawsuit – you could go to trial and lose, and end up with nothing – you could have IPOfferings represent you in the sale of your patent. A patent that has Claim Charts that document infringement of the patent is a very valuable asset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selling a patent with documented infringement reduces litigation risk but may yield less money than winning a lawsuit; evaluate options and tradeoffs (risk of trial vs. certain but smaller proceeds from sale/licensing).
